ai.description: This small frog reaches 22–26 mm. It is brown with a distinct dark interorbital triangle and a pale yellow belly. Key features include granular skin and a lack of webbing on the fingers.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes longchuanensis* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow or golden-yellow groin and hidden surfaces of the thighs, which lack the dark mottling found in similar Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: The Longchuan Bubble-nest Frog inhabits subtropical evergreen forests and bamboo thickets, typically found at elevations between 1,200 and 1,600 meters.
ai.behavior: The Longchuan bubble-nest frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining active at night to forage for small insects among forest vegetation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes longchuanensis* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They breed during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in terrestrial nests.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Longchuan Bubble-nest Frog is found in the subtropical forests of Arunachal Pradesh, India, at elevations ranging from approximately 1,200 to 1,600 meters.
ai.callDescription: The call of *Raorchestes longchuanensis* consists of a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard from vegetation in humid forest habitats.
